UNDERSTANDING THE MASS The Pray er After Communion: "Let Us Pray" What is Happening Communion has been received. The sacred vessels are quietly purified. A moment of silence settles over the congregation and then the priest says once more: "Let us pray." The Prayer After Communion is brief, almost understated. Yet it carries something important: it asks God that what we have just received might bear fruit in our lives. We did not simply attend a ceremony. Something happened. The prayer acknowledges this and asks that it not stop here - that the grace of the Eucharist might continue working in us as we return to ordinary life. How We Shou ld Respond This prayer is easily missed - we are still settling after Communion, perhaps still absorbed in personal thanksgiving. But it deserves our attention. It is the Church's collective voice asking: "Lord, may this change us." That is a prayer worth making our own. Not just at Mass, but in the moments after - in the car, on the walk home, over Sunday lunch. Living This at Mass After Mass this Sunday, carry the question with you: what am I asking God to do with what I have just received? The Eucharist is not a conclusion - it is a commissioning. The Prayer After Communion points us forward, back into the world, changed. November Reflection Death - Resurrection We think of death as coming to destroy; Let us rather picture Christ as coming to save. We think of death as ending; Let us rather think of life as beginning. We think of losing; Let us think of gaining. We think of parting; Let us think of meeting. And as the voice of death whispers: "You must go from earth." Let us hear the voice of Christ saying: "You are but coming to me." Amen. POPE LEOXIV Wherever we may find ourselves, by opening our hearts to God we can live out the fundamental relationship that enables every human being to reflect the divine image. Through our bond with the Trinity, our hearts are healed and elevated by grace; and we can then open ourselves to our brothers and sisters in order to heal, love, and serve them with the goodness of the Lord. 21st/ 22nd November 20 26

NEW STAINED GLASS WINDOWS Two new stained glass windows have been installed in our parish church to commemorate the worldwide Aids epidemic. The windows are an opportunity to remember in prayer and reflection all those who died of Aids, all those in Church and State who cared for them and ail family and friends who grieve the great loss of loved ones. The windows have been funded by a very kind parish benefactor and constructed by Capital Glass of Leonards Corner. We will hold a prayer service on United Nations World Aids Day the 1° December to mark their installation. NOVEMBER ALTAR LIST OF THE DEAD ENVELOPES are available in the church and can be returned to any member of the Parish Team or placed in the safe in the Church. Please remember in your prayers deceased Marist Fathers who worked in this parish: Jim Connington, Tim Kenny, Gus O Herlihy, Ray Murray, Jimmy Carr, Bobby Kelly, Liam Deaton & Jim O Connell. THE NOVEMBER TREE OF REMEMBRANCE is in place now near the entrance to the church. You are invited to write the names of your deceased relatives and friends on the labels and to place them on the tree for prayerful remembrance by the parishioners and friends of St. Teresa’s. November is also a lovely time to visit a loved one’s grave. RECENTLY BAPTISED We congratulate Luke Phillips who was baptised into the Christian community recently. We wish every good grace on him as he grows in love & knowledge of God.
